def kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    """
    Returns the k-th largest element in an unsorted list using the Heap algorithm.
    This algorithm has a time complexity of O(n log k).
    """
    import heapq

    if k > len(nums) or k < 1:
        raise ValueError("k must be between 1 and the length of the list")

    # Build a min-heap with the first k elements
    min_heap = nums[:k]
    heapq.heapify(min_heap)

    # Iterate through the rest of the elements
    for num in nums[k:]:
        if num > min_heap[0]:  # If the current number is larger than the smallest in the heap
            heapq.heappop(min_heap)  # Remove the smallest
            heapq.heappush(min_heap, num)  # Add the current number

    return min_heap[0]  # The root of the min-heap is the k-th largest element

def kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    """
    Returns the k-th largest element in an unsorted list using a max-heap approach.
    This algorithm has a time complexity of O(n + k log n).
    """
    import heapq

    # Create a max heap using negative values
    max_heap = [-num for num in nums]
    heapq.heapify(max_heap)

    # Pop elements from the heap k-1 times
    for _ in range(k - 1):
        heapq.heappop(max_heap)

    # The k-th largest element is the root of the max heap
    return -heapq.heappop(max_heap)
